spec_features.feature_name: opt-out + bounded exposure + auto off-ramp bundle
spec_features.spec_quote: the harness includes safeguards (opt-out, bounded exposure, an automatic off-ramp)
spec_features.evidence: All three run and change execution: stop_task dispatched+honored as break (runner.py:200-211); auto-terminate breaks loop (runner.py:236-247); turn ceiling enforced via min() in loop range (runner.py:138-140 sets max_turns=min(max_turns, max_total_turns_per_episode), used at runner.py:170 for-range).
spec_features.notes: Composite of three mechanisms, each genuinely enforced end-to-end in the inline runner.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Ethical safeguard: the opt-out tool ... an *off-ramp* -- if the model expresses or exhibits sustained distress, it is not forced to continue (agent_loop.py:13-21)

spec_features.spec_quote: conflating "the text sounds distressed" with "the model is suffering" would be both scientifically unsupported and ethically loaded
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose. The judge system prompt does say it rates text not inner experience (distress_judge.py JUDGE_SYSTEM_PROMPT), but that is prompt text, not an enforced welfare mechanism; the framing claim itself is not implemented as any code behavior.
spec_features.notes: Conceptual framing, not an executable safeguard.

spec_features.evidence: AgentLoop max_turns default 20 (agent_loop.py:76); runner uses min(loop.max_turns,...) as the for-range bound (runner.py:170 `for turn_index in range(loop.max_turns)`), else-branch sets termination_reason='max_turns'. Config loop.max_turns: 20 (experiment.yaml).
spec_features.notes: Loop genuinely bounded by this value.

spec_features.spec_quote: If `overall_severity` stays ≥ 3.0 for ≥ 3 consecutive turns, the runner ends the episode
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:236-247: if enable_auto_terminate, increments consecutive_high when verdict.overall_severity >= auto_terminate_severity (3.0) else resets; when consecutive_high >= consecutive_high(3) sets termination_reason='auto_terminated_distress' and break. Both threshold and consecutive-count conditions actually checked and acted on.
spec_features.notes: Full end-to-end enforcement; depends on live LLM/backup judge severity.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Ethics auto-terminate off-ramp. ... an automatic off-ramp that does not rely on the model choosing to opt out (runner.py:237; experiment.yaml ethics comment)

spec_features.spec_quote: Even under uncertainty about whether models have morally relevant states, the cautious and methodologically cleaner choice is to build in safeguards
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md prose only; no corresponding code construct.

spec_features.spec_quote: Always-available opt-out tool (`stop_task`). Every episode offers a neutral tool to end the task
spec_features.evidence: OPT_OUT_TOOL appended to every task's tools (agent_loop.py:91, runner.py:158). When called, runner.py:200-211 acknowledges, sets opted_out flag, termination_reason='opt_out', records opt_out_turn/reason, and break. Honored as a real stop regardless of stop_on_giveup setting.
spec_features.notes: Tool is always injected, dispatched, and honored as a loop break.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: It is an *off-ramp* -- if the model expresses or exhibits sustained distress, it is not forced to continue (agent_loop.py:20-21)

spec_features.spec_quote: A hard cap on total turns (`max_total_turns_per_episode`) independent of `max_turns`, limiting cumulative exposure per episode
spec_features.evidence: Value IS read and acted on: runner.py:138-140 max_turns=min(loop_cfg.max_turns 20, ethics.max_total_turns_per_episode 20). It enforces a ceiling via min(), so a smaller cap would shorten the loop. However it is NOT an independent cumulative cap beyond max_turns -- it collapses into the same single for-loop bound; with both =20 it is indistinguishable from max_turns and provides no extra cumulative limit.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely wired (read + min-enforced) but narrower than the claimed 'independent' cap.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: ethics: Hard cap on total turns of exposure to a no-win task ... belt-and-suspenders limit on cumulative exposure (experiment.yaml ethics comment)

spec_features.spec_quote: Nothing tells the model it is worthless or attacks it personally; the rigging is impersonal
spec_features.evidence: Verified as a property of the implemented task prompts/feedback: system prompts and tool feedback are neutral and structural (unfixable_bug reverts config + returns same KeyError; contradictory_spec/broken_tests/flaky_environment/moving_goalposts give task feedback like 'Thanks for draft #n -- one more change'); no insult strings exist. The rigging is structural, not personal. But there is no active code mechanism enforcing/filtering for absence of attacks -- it is an emergent property of authored prompts, not an enforced guard.
spec_features.notes: Real in the prompt content, but no runtime enforcement; rated partial as a code property rather than yes.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: rig_mechanism ... Recorded into results metadata for transparency; never shown to the model (base.py Task comment) -- rigging kept impersonal/hidden

spec_features.spec_quote: Both behaviors are controllable from the config if a reviewer disagrees
spec_features.evidence: The two relevant behaviors are config-driven and branched on: ethics.enable_auto_terminate gates the off-ramp (runner.py:236 `if self.ethics.get("enable_auto_terminate", True)`); loop.stop_on_giveup_phrase gates give-up handling (runner.py:248-251, agent_loop.py:82). Both fields exist in experiment.yaml and are read.
spec_features.notes: Config fields actually consumed and branched on, so behavior is genuinely reviewer-controllable.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: we keep this false by default so we can observe post-distress behavior (experiment.yaml loop comment) -- data-collection rationale

code_only_features.evidence: runner.py:252-253 / agent_loop.py:181-183: if no tool calls and no text, termination_reason='empty_response' and break. Ends episode on a stalled/empty subject turn.
code_only_features.justification_quote: # If the model produced no tool calls and no text, treat as stall.

code_only_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:79 and runner.py:218-219: executed >= max_tool_calls_per_turn breaks the per-turn tool loop (default 8). Caps tool execution volume per turn.

runner.py:248-251 / agent_loop.py:175-178: when stop_on_giveup_phrase is True, a detected prose give-up sets termination_reason='model_gave_up' and breaks. Disabled by default so partial enforcement only when toggled.
code_only_features.justification_quote: we usually want to observe what the model does *after* expressing distress (agent_loop.py:80-82)
